title: Sixteenth of June: the event date under inelastic dark matter and under background
question: What is the likelihood ratio of the 16 June 2023 event date under time-flat backgrounds versus annually modulating inelastic (delta = 100-380 keV) and elastic signals given the 220-live-day run, and how much information does the date carry?
headline_result: The date multiplies the odds for m = 1000 GeV inelastic DM over flat backgrounds by 1.41 (delta = 300 keV), 2.08 (350) and 2.55 (380 keV) but by 0.98 for elastic SI; it is a p = 0.086 (1.4 sigma) observation worth 0.04-0.3 nats, needing ~107 (delta = 300) or ~18 (350 keV) events for 3 sigma from dates alone; delta_max(248 keV, 1000 GeV) rises from 376 to 387 keV on 16 June.
model_or_mechanism: annual modulation of O1 elastic and inelastic (m = 1000 GeV) WimPyDD rates in the LZ ROI; single-event time-PDF likelihood ratio; KL information content
confidence: high for LR and kinematics; medium for N_3sigma (unpublished livetime, flat-background assumption) [coordinator note, step 066: P006 ran before the wd_halo v_min-grid fix (step 047); P020 finds its delta=350/380 keV time-PDFs flatter than a recomputation; LRs at delta<=350 keV accurate to 20-30%]
